params.body:
1,766 live concepts are lexical twins of another concept by the desk's own matcher, carrying 2,439 mentions between them: "generational-meta-discourse-awareness" beside "generational discourse meta-awareness", "esports rivalry fandom" beside "esports team rivalry fandom". They are not near-misses, they are the same words in a different order, which is what `concept-match` was written to catch at birth. These are the ones born before it existed on 3 September.

A twin is not harmless. It splits the evidence under a reading, it halves the count that decides whether a concept is confirmed, and this morning it offered the same research question twice on the Sources page, which is where it finally became visible.

**What a fold has to move is more than it looks.** A concept is referenced in seven places and in three shapes: a plain id in mentions and edges, an array of ids in patterns, an array of `{_ref}` objects in insights, two poles on a tension, one id on an article's evidence, an array on a quality snapshot. Miss one and the fold leaves a reference nobody can resolve, which is exactly the fault the graph drain exists to clean up. One transaction per twin, because half a fold is a concept whose mentions moved and whose patterns did not, and that reads as evidence disappearing.

**The keeper's count is recounted, never summed.** Twins share signals. Folding the heaviest pair on a copy of the live database gave the keeper 477 mentions where a sum would have claimed 507: thirty signals mentioned both, and adding them up would have invented evidence.

**The twin is archived and marked, not deleted.** The matcher deliberately keeps archived concepts so a proposal in the same words revives the old row rather than minting a fresh twin. Without a `merged_into` marker the next enrich run would revive exactly what was folded, so the vocabulary now answers with the keeper for a folded row.

**A tension whose poles fold into each other is left standing and reported.** An editor wrote it, and a pole that folded is something for a person to look at, not a row for a script to remove.

Rehearsed on a copy of the live database: the heaviest five moved 165 mentions, 311 edges, 36 patterns, 318 insights and 120 snapshots, with nothing left pointing at a twin and no self-edges anywhere.

Five tests covering every shape, the shared-signal recount and the revival trap. Suite 679 green.

Dry by default and NOT scheduled: this is a one-off for what was born before the matcher, and after it the matcher prevents the next one. Run `bin/concept-fold.mjs` to read the plan, `--limit N` to take the heaviest few first.
params.title: Two names for one thing: the fold
